note: Literature explicitly documents two distinct clinical subtypes of isolated CLN3-associated retinal degeneration based on age of onset, macular involvement/foveal preservation, and progression to legal blindness.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 15 patients with isolated CLN3-linked retinal degeneration, two distinct disease patterns were identified: a mild rod-cone dystrophy of middle-age onset (n=6) reaching legal blindness in the 70s, and a severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes (n=9) reaching legal blindness in the 40s.

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: Two distinct patterns of retinal disease could be identified: a mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset (n = 6; legal blindness threshold reached by 70s) and a severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes (n = 9; legal blindness threshold reached by 40s).

evidence.text: Evaluation of 10 patients with isolated CLN3 retinal disease identified 4 with progressive late-onset rod-cone dystrophy displaying focal foveal preservation on OCT and 6 with earlier-onset rod-cone dystrophy showing significant photoreceptor loss.

source.title: Detailed Clinical Phenotype and Molecular Genetic Findings in CLN3-Associated Isolated Retinal Degeneration
source.quote: Of the 10 patients, 4 had a progressive late-onset rod-cone dystrophy, with a mean (range) age at onset of 29.7 (20-40) years, and 6 had an earlier onset rod-cone dystrophy, with a mean (range) age at onset of 12.1 (7-17) years. Ophthalmoscopic examination features included macular edema, mild intraretinal pigment migration, and widespread atrophy in advanced disease. Optical coherence tomography imaging demonstrated significant photoreceptor loss except in patients with late-onset disease who had a focal preservation of the ellipsoid zone and outer nuclear layer in the fovea.
